Description:
The week view grid renders columns Sunday → Saturday. The PRD and story SV-8686 Ready for QA define the week as a Mon–Sun grid. The sidebar mini calendar on the same screen is already Monday-first, so the page shows two different week orders at once.

Steps to Reproduce:
1. Open http://sv8685.qa.shopview.com and go to Schedule.
2. Select the Week view.
3. Compare the grid's first column with the mini calendar's first column.

Expected Result: Week grid columns are ordered Monday → Sunday (Saturday/Sunday still individually toggleable via View Options).

Actual Result: Week grid columns are ordered Sunday → Saturday; mini calendar is Monday-first on the same screen.

Bilal Muzamil

Description

The PRD requires the shift modal to show estimated hours with inline edit, and the scheduled line to show labor and total figures. The estimated hours value is displayed but cannot be edited, and no labor or total figures appear on the line.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Open the Schedule module
  2. Go to the week of Aug 2 to 8, 2026
  3. Click the Pamill Paving shift on the Jose Young row, Sunday Aug 2
  4. Click the 1h value on the "Replace - Rear ramp handles" line
  5. Look at the line row for labor and total figures

Expected Result

Clicking the estimated hours opens an inline edit control so the value can be changed. The line row shows labor and total figures.

Actual Result

The estimated hours value is not clickable or editable. The line row shows only 1h and an Authorized badge, with no labor or total figures.
Bilal Muzamil

screen-capture (27).webm

fields.summary: Shift detail modal: estimated hours is not editable and line labor/total figures are missing

renderedFields.description:
Description

A shift scheduled on Sunday for a technician who is not working weekends is not detected as a conflict. No warning icon on the block, no conflict pill in the toolbar, and no conflict banner in the modal. The PRD lists Weekend shift as a conflict type.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Open the Schedule module
  2. Go to the week of Aug 2 to 8, 2026
  3. Look at the Pamill Paving shift on the Jose Young row, Sunday Aug 2, 07:00 AM to 08:00 AM
  4. Check the block for a warning icon
  5. Check the toolbar for a conflict pill
  6. Click the block and check the modal for a conflict banner

Expected Result

The shift is flagged as a Weekend shift conflict. A warning icon shows on the block, the toolbar conflict pill shows a count and lists it in the dropdown, and the modal shows a conflict banner with an Adjust action.

Actual Result

No warning icon, no conflict pill, and no conflict banner. The shift is treated as normal even though the technician is set to Not working on Sunday.

screen-capture (28).webm

fields.summary: Weekend shift is not flagged as a conflict
Schedule — Technician Scheduling Module

Description

The start and end time pickers in the shift modal let you pick any minute value. The PRD requires 15-minute increments, and the design shows a dropdown stepping 6:45, 7:00, 7:15, 7:30. Secondary issue: in QA the picker only opens from the clock icon, while in the design clicking the time field itself opens it.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Open the Schedule module, week of Aug 2 to 8, 2026
  2. Click any shift block to open the modal
  3. Click the clock icon in the start time field
  4. Look at the minute column

Expected Result

The picker offers 15-minute increments only, such as 7:00, 7:15, 7:30, 7:45, and it opens when the time field is clicked.

Actual Result

The minute column lists every minute, 00, 01, 02, 03, 04, 05 and so on, so any minute can be selected. The picker also opens only from the clock icon, not by clicking the field.

PRD:

screen-capture (29).webm

fields.summary: Shift time picker allows any minute instead of 15-minute increments

Description

The shift tooltip and shift detail modal show TIME LOGGED as 1h / 1h with a full progress bar, but the work order shows Actual 0.00 of 1.00 and Progress 0%. No time has been clocked against the line, so the schedule is reporting work that never happened.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Open WO S8685-12876 and note line 1 shows Actual/Estimate 0.00 / 1.00 and Progress 0%
  2. Open the Schedule module, week of Aug 2 to 8, 2026
  3. Hover the Pamill Paving shift on the Jose Young row, Sunday Aug 2
  4. Also click the block to open the modal
  5. Compare the TIME LOGGED values

Expected Result

Time logged reflects actual clocked time, so it shows 0h / 1h with an empty progress bar.

Actual Result

Both the tooltip and the modal show 1h / 1h with a full progress bar, indicating the line is complete while the work order reports 0% and zero actual hours.

screen-capture (30).webm

fields.summary: Schedule shows time logged as complete when nothing has been clocked

renderedFields.description:
Description

Day view always opens with the timeline at 12 AM. It should scroll so the working-day start sits at the left edge with a small buffer before it. Shop business hours are off and Jose Young's hours start at 7:00 AM, so the timeline should open near 6:30 AM.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Open the Schedule module
  2. Click Day
  3. Note the leftmost time column
  4. Click the forward arrow to move to the next day
  5. Note the leftmost time column again

Expected Result

On load and on day navigation the timeline auto-scrolls so the working-day start is at the left edge, showing roughly 6:30 AM first.

Actual Result

The timeline starts at 12 AM on load and stays at 12 AM after navigating to the next day. The user has to scroll manually to reach working hours.

PRD:

screen-capture (32).webm

fields.summary: Day view does not auto-scroll to the working-day start

renderedFields.description:
Description

The capacity tooltip gives every technician their normal daily capacity on weekends, even when their staff record says Not working. Sunday Aug 2 shows the same 168h total capacity as Thursday Aug 6, a normal working day. Capacity should be the sum of the technicians' actual working hours for that day..

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Open the Schedule module, Week view, week of Aug 2 to 8, 2026
  2. Hover the capacity bar under Thursday Aug 6 and note the total capacity
  3. Hover the capacity bar under Sunday Aug 2
  4. Compare the totals and Jose Young's capacity

Expected Result

Sunday capacity only counts technicians who work Sunday. Since nobody has Sunday hours, the total is 0h and Jose is not listed with a 12h capacity.

Actual Result

Sunday shows 31.7h assigned of 168h capacity, the same capacity as Thursday. Jose is listed as 1.2h / 12h even though Sunday is Not working for him.

PRD:

fields.summary: Capacity bar counts full capacity on days technicians are not working
Schedule — Technician Scheduling Module

  3. Drag the "Replace - Windshield button" line over a technician cell and hold it there
  4. Observe the grid before releasing

Expected Result

The target cell highlights and a ghost block showing the line name and hours follows the cursor.

Actual Result

Nothing is shown during the drag. The block appears only after the mouse is released.

renderedFields.description:
Description

The sidebar search matches the numeric part of a work order number but not the full number shown on the card. Typing S8685-9379 returns "No schedulable work orders match this filter", while typing 9379 returns the card. The spec says the search matches on WO number.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Open the Schedule module
  2. In the sidebar search type S8685-9379
  3. Note the result
  4. Clear the search and type 9379
  5. Note the result

Expected Result

Both searches return the S8685-9379 Xiriver Apparel card, since S8685-9379 is the number displayed on the card.

Actual Result

S8685-9379 returns "No schedulable work orders match this filter". 9379 returns the card. Users copying the number as displayed get no results.

PRD:

screen-capture (34).webm

fields.summary: Sidebar search returns no results when you type the full work order number
